leverage_rationale: WebMCP is deeply embedded in a browser Python IDE: agents can edit and run cells/files, inspect variables, install packages, debug, and manipulate analysis artifacts through a large structured tool surface.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes 49 tools covering notebook, file, kernel, DataFrame, chart, and package operations.

Live observation opened the browser IDE and accepted New notebook.
execution_rationale: The live IDE loaded coherently and the notebook creation action succeeded, matching the claimed browser workspace; the full data-analysis loop was supported by video rather than the short live action.
execution_evidence: Live observation: New notebook succeeded and editor/project navigation remained available.
Video transcript reports dataset fetch, pandas execution, charting, and linked tool activity.
impact_rationale: An in-browser, local-first research workspace that removes context switching can substantially improve analysis workflows and privacy, though impact is bounded by the notebook's browser/runtime constraints.
impact_evidence: Submission identifies context switching among Jupyter, documentation, and terminal as the problem.
Python runs in Pyodide with no kernel server and no data leaving the machine, according to submission and video transcript.
creativity_rationale: The combination of a full browser notebook IDE and agent-operable structured research tools is unusually complete and specific, extending WebMCP into active computational collaboration.
creativity_evidence: 49 purpose-built tools span code, files, execution, variables, DataFrames, charts, and debugging.
Agent actions are linked to the cells they touched while the notebook remains user-owned.
s2_notes: Live notebook creation verified; full agent-analysis behavior is additionally supported by the supplied video transcript.
advance_reason: Deep WebMCP integration, coherent live workspace, and strong evidence of end-to-end notebook collaboration.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used as a bounded governance protocol for reading evidence, proposing an exact change, applying only an approved payload, and verifying browser behavior, with no approval tool.
leverage_evidence: Submission and video describe four explicit read/propose/apply/verify tools and guarded revisioned writes.
Live observation shows observe, precedent, proposal, review, apply, and verify stages with a visible human boundary.
execution_rationale: The live rehearsal advanced coherently in the real dialog workflow and matched the claimed staged governance model; the observation did not itself complete approval/application.
execution_evidence: Live observation: Run opening rehearsal succeeded and produced a captured after-state.
Observation confirms proposal and guarded-application controls remained visible and no destructive change was applied.
Video transcript reports approval, revision advance, and six passing verification checks.
impact_rationale: Making accessibility changes reviewable, reversible, and evidence-backed can reduce dangerous agent overreach in real product workflows, with a clear transfer beyond this focus example.
impact_evidence: Submission frames the concrete destructive-dialog focus mismatch and reviewer approval requirement.
Workflow records exact diff, digest, base revision, receipt, and rehearsal checks.
creativity_rationale: The explicit no-approval-tool design and immutable proposal-to-review-to-apply contract is a highly distinctive WebMCP treatment of human authority and browser changes.
creativity_evidence: Agent cannot manufacture authority; only visible UI-mediated approval authorizes application.
Protocol makes browser/agent/reviewer handoffs inspectable and testable.
s2_notes: Live rehearsal was verified and the supplied video provides detailed evidence for the complete guarded workflow.
advance_reason: Exceptional governance-oriented WebMCP design with coherent live rehearsal and strong end-to-end video evidence.
